newsitem.title: JAPAN: France sees budget deficit cut to 2 pct after 1998.
newsitem.headline: France sees budget deficit cut to 2 pct after 1998.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said he expects France's fiscal deficit to fall incrementally to two percent after 1998, a Japanese financial daily reported on Friday.
But ultimately France aims to balance the budget, the Nihon Keizai Shimbun quoted Arthuis as saying in an interview with the paper conducted in Paris on Thursday.

The paper did not say whether Arthuis gave a timetable for a balanced budget, but added that he predicted a fiscal deficit of three percent of gross domestic product for next year -- just enough to pass the Maastricht criteria.
Meeting Maastricht criteria is a precondition for the franc's admittance into European monetary union.
The paper also quoted Arthuis as saying that the deficit should be down to 2.8 percent in 1998.
In order to balance the budget, France would seek to reduce the number of public workers on its government payroll and streamline ministries where jurisdictions overlap, he was quoted as saying.
